1. Who We Are
b

Indro Labs Inc. (“Indro Labs,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) provides a software-as-a-service transportation-coordination platform (the “Platform,” referred to in our Software-as-a-Service Terms of Service as the “Indro Labs SaaS Services”) used by organizations (“Customers”) to schedule, dispatch, and track rides for the people they serve. We also operate our marketing website at https://www.indrolabs.ca/ (the “Website”).
Indro Labs is based in Calgary, Alberta.

This Privacy Policy (the “Policy”) is published on the Website at https://www.indrolabs.ca/privacy. It is the privacy policy referred to in the Website Terms of Use. It is separate from the Software-as-a-Service Terms of Service (the “Terms of Service”), which govern the Platform and are made available on the Platform itself. The Terms of Service contain their own Privacy section (Section 4 of that Agreement); this Policy is the standalone, publicly accessible statement of our information practices. The French version of this Policy is available at https://www.indrolabs.ca/fr/privacy. La version française de la présente politique est disponible à https://www.indrolabs.ca/fr/privacy.
2. Scope
b

This Policy describes how Indro Labs collects, uses, discloses, and safeguards personal information in connection with (a) the Platform and (b) the Website. For the Platform, it applies to Customer organizations and to the individuals a Customer enrolls or serves through the Platform — including administrators, drivers, riders (including guests who book a ride through a Customer's public booking page), and the family members or caregivers (“members”) a Customer or rider may add to a rider's record. For the Website, it applies to visitors to the Website (see Section 6).

The Platform is currently offered for use within Canada, excluding Quebec. Under the Terms of Service, Customers may access and use the Platform only in Canada unless we approve another territory in writing, and we are not actively selling into or onboarding organizations based in Quebec at this stage.

This Policy does not replace or limit the Terms of Service or any Order Form between Indro Labs and a Customer, which govern the commercial and legal relationship between the parties. Where this Policy and the Terms of Service address the same subject, the Terms of Service govern the contractual relationship; this Policy describes our actual information practices.
3. Our Role as a Service Provider
b

Indro Labs provides the Platform as a business-to-business (B2B) software-as-a-service offering. Individuals do not enter into an agreement with us to use the Platform. A Customer organization enrolls its own riders, drivers, and administrators and directs how the Platform is used for its operations. Where a Customer makes its public booking page available, riders and guests can also book a ride, or create a rider account, directly with that Customer through the Platform.

In this relationship, Indro Labs acts as a service provider processing personal information on behalf of, and under the direction of, the Customer that determines why that information is collected and how it is used in the Customer's own operations (for example, deciding which riders to enroll, what trips to schedule, and who receives notifications). Under the Terms of Service, we process the personal information we handle for a Customer (“Customer Personal Information”) only to fulfil our obligations and exercise our rights under the Agreement, or as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law. We also process limited information for our own purposes, as described in Section 8 — primarily security, billing, support, and legal compliance.
4. The Customer's Role and Responsibilities
b

Under the Terms of Service, the Customer is responsible for, among other things: obtaining and providing all consents and notices needed for its own collection and use of personal information about its riders, drivers, and other Permitted Users (including End Users); the accuracy, quality, and legality of the data it enters into the Platform and its and its Permitted Users' use of that data; and complying with Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL) for any commercial electronic messages it sends or causes to be sent. The Terms of Service also require each Customer to maintain and make available to its Permitted Users a public-facing privacy policy that accurately describes how it processes their personal information, explains that it has partnered with Indro Labs as a service provider, and directs readers to this Policy for information about how Indro Labs processes personal information.

A Customer's own privacy notice will explain that the Customer is directly accountable to you for the protection and processing of the information used to access your account. That does not change our own responsibility to safeguard the personal information in our custody and to honour the commitments in this Policy.

If you are a rider, driver, family member/caregiver, or other individual using the Platform through an organization, your primary point of contact for privacy questions about your own information is that organization — though you may also contact us using the details in Section 26.
5. Information We Collect Through the Platform
b
The following describes the categories of personal information the Platform currently collects and processes.
5.1 Account and organization-user information
b
Name, email address, an optional phone number, and password (stored only as a secure one-way hash, never in plain text) for administrators and for any other user who has a Platform account.
A profile photo, if the user chooses to add one.
Whether the user's email address has been verified, and whether the account has been deactivated or suspended.
5.2 Rider information
b
Name, phone number, and (optionally) email address.
A profile photo, if added.
Accessibility or transportation-need indicators (whether a larger vehicle or additional wait time is required) — see Section 13.
Saved pickup/destination places (label, address, and coordinates), and trip history — see Section 10.
Notification preferences, including whether the rider has opted out of SMS messages — see Section 14.
If the rider has a Platform account (created by the rider on a Customer's booking page, or set up by the Customer), the account information in Section 5.1.

Guests who book without an account provide their first and last name, phone number, email address, pickup and destination, pickup time, and (optionally) the accessibility indicators above. This information is kept as a rider record within the Customer's organization.
5.3 Driver information
b
Name, email address, phone number, driver's licence number, and licence expiry date.
Vehicle information associated with the driver (make, model, year, licence plate).
Work schedule and availability information, and notification preferences.
Whether the driver's account has been suspended.
5.4 Family member / caregiver (“member”) information
b

Name, phone number and/or email address of a family member or caregiver added to a rider's record, the nature of the relationship (for example, family member or caregiver), and that person's notification preferences (including whether they have opted in to live-tracking links and whether they have opted out of SMS messages).
This information is entered by the Customer organization or the rider on the member's behalf — the member does not create an account or interact with us directly to provide it.
5.5 Location and trip information
b

Trip records include pickup and destination addresses and coordinates, the driver's declared starting location, the assigned driver and vehicle, the stages and times of the trip (for example, en route, arrived, passenger on board, completed), distance and fare where pricing is configured, and any cancellation or no-show information. See Section 10 (Location Information) for a dedicated description of location data, which is one of the more significant categories of information the Platform handles.
5.6 Payment-related information
b

See Section 15. In short, payment card details are collected directly by our payment processor, not by us; we keep only the reference identifiers and status information needed to reconcile payments with trips.
5.7 Technical and security information
b

IP address, recorded together with authentication events (sign-in successes and failures, password changes and resets, invitation acceptance, email verification, and sign-out) for security monitoring and fraud detection.

A record of each Terms of Service acceptance made by a Customer's authorized administrator: which user, for which Customer, which version of the Terms of Service, when, the IP address and browser/device information (user-agent string) at the time, and a hash of the text that was displayed. This is the only place the Platform currently records browser/device information.

Operational and error logs generated by the Platform's hosting environment. These logs are not intended to hold personal information, but individual entries (for example, an error message about a specific booking) may incidentally include identifiers such as an email address.
An internal record each time an authorized Indro Labs staff member views a Customer's account as one of its users for support purposes.
5.8 Support requests
b

If a user contacts support through the Platform's Help function, we collect the user's name, email address, and phone number (if provided), their role and organization, and the message they write. A copy of the request is emailed to our support inbox and, where configured, posted to an internal Slack channel so our team can respond.
6. Information We Collect Through the Marketing Website
b
You do not need to give us any personal information to browse the Website. The Website does not currently offer user accounts, features for posting content, or a newsletter or mailing-list sign-up.

Book a demo. The Contact page embeds a scheduling tool provided by Calendly. Information you enter to book a time (for example, your name, email address, and meeting details) is collected by Calendly and made available to us so we can hold the meeting. Calendly's own privacy policy also applies.
Email. If you email us at info@indrolabs.ca, we receive your email address and whatever you include in your message.

Technical requests. Loading the Website causes your browser to request fonts from Google Fonts and resources from Calendly, so those providers receive your IP address and standard browser request information. Our hosting provider also handles the technical requests needed to deliver Website pages.

Browser storage. The Website uses your browser's session storage to remember that the “book a demo” pop-up has already been shown during your visit, so it is not shown repeatedly. This contains no personal information and is cleared when your browsing session ends.

The Website's own code does not include analytics, advertising, or social-media tracking tools. Third-party content embedded in the Website (such as Calendly) may set its own cookies or similar technologies, subject to that provider's own policies. The Website also contains links to third-party websites (for example, LinkedIn and our partners); we do not control those sites, and their own privacy policies apply.
We use information you give us through the Website to respond to you, schedule and hold demos, and operate and secure the Website. We do not sell it.
7. How We Collect Information
b
Directly from the Customer organization, when an administrator enters rider, driver, or member information.
From riders, guests, drivers, and members, when they book a ride, create or update an account or profile, or contact support — including guests who have no pre-existing account.
Automatically, through use of the Platform (for example, trip timestamps, vehicle location during an active trip, and authentication logs).
From our service providers, such as payment status and identifiers from Stripe, and delivery status and opt-out replies (such as STOP) from Twilio.
For the Website, as described in Section 6.
8. Purposes of Collection and Use
b
We use personal information for the following purposes:
Operating the Platform: scheduling and dispatching trips, coordinating drivers and vehicles, and providing live trip status.
Communications: sending SMS and email notifications related to bookings, trip status, and account activity.
Payments: processing and reconciling payment for rides, where that feature is in use.
Security and fraud prevention: authenticating users, monitoring for suspicious activity, keeping records of Terms of Service acceptance, and investigating security incidents.
Customer support: responding to support requests from Customers and their users, and to enquiries received through the Website.
Legal compliance: meeting our own legal, accounting, and regulatory obligations.
We do not sell personal information to third parties, and we do not use rider, driver, or member information collected through the Platform to serve targeted advertising.

Under the Terms of Service, Indro Labs may create “Usage Data” (information about how individuals use the Platform) and “Anonymous Data” (data that is not identifiable as to any individual and is not personal information), and may use them for any purpose. The Terms of Service also state that the licence they give us to use Customer data to develop and improve our offering does not extend to Customer Personal Information.

We do not currently use trip, location, or rider data to train machine-learning or artificial-intelligence models. If this changes in the future, we will update this Policy and, where required, seek appropriate consent before doing so.
9. Consent and the Customer's Responsibility
b

For personal information that a Customer collects and provides to us for processing on the Customer's behalf, the Customer is responsible for obtaining any consent and providing any notice required by applicable law for its own collection and use of that information. Under the Terms of Service, the Customer has represented and warranted that it has obtained, and will continue to obtain, all necessary consents and provided all necessary notices for that collection and use (see Section 4).

Where we process information for our own purposes described in Section 8 (for example, security logging or billing), we do so as necessary to operate and secure the Platform, administer our relationship with Customers, and comply with our legal obligations, as permitted by applicable law.
If you contact us through the Website, you do so voluntarily, and we use the information you provide to respond to you.
10. Location Information
b
The Platform handles several distinct types of location information, described separately here because they carry different sensitivity and are handled differently:
10.1 Planned locations
b

Pickup and destination addresses (and their coordinates) entered when booking a trip, and any places a user chooses to save for faster re-booking. Saved-place labels are free text chosen by the user; a label can incidentally reveal sensitive information, such as the name of a medical clinic, even though the field itself is not a structured medical-information field.
10.2 Historical trip locations
b
Pickup and destination addresses, and the driver's starting location, are retained as part of each trip's record for operational and billing purposes. See Section 22 for retention.
10.3 Real-time vehicle location
b

While a trip is in progress, the Platform records the vehicle's current location, as reported through the driver's use of the Platform, to support live tracking and dispatch. Only the most recent position for each vehicle is stored; it is overwritten with each update, and the Platform does not keep a running history of a vehicle's movements. Customer administrators can see live vehicle locations, and the rider and others holding a tracking link can see the location of the vehicle assigned to that trip.
10.4 Public tracking links
b
See Section 11 for a dedicated description of the tracking-link feature, which is a distinct way location information can be shared.
11. Public Tracking Links
b

A Customer administrator, or the driver assigned to a trip, can create a tracking link for that trip. Anyone who has the link can open it without signing in, and the person who creates a link decides whom to share it with. The link shows a single trip: the rider's first name, the pickup and destination addresses, the trip's status, and the vehicle's current location and when it was last updated. It does not show the rider's account, other trips, or anything else in the Customer's organization.

A tracking link stops working 24 hours after it is created. The tracking page itself displays a reminder that anyone with the link can see the trip's live location. Because access depends only on possession of the link, links should be shared only with people who should see the trip. When the page displays a map, the viewer's browser also connects to Mapbox (see Section 16).
12. Information Relating to Minors
b

The Platform is designed to support Customer use cases where the person being transported is a minor — for example, a school or daycare arranging transportation for children — and where the minor does not have their own Platform account. In that configuration, the minor is recorded as a rider (name and any accessibility/transportation-need information), and a parent, guardian, or caregiver is recorded as a “member” who receives trip notifications and tracking links on the minor's behalf.

We rely on the Customer organization to have obtained any consent or authorization required by applicable law from a parent or guardian before enrolling a minor as a rider, consistent with the Customer's responsibilities in Section 4. We do not independently verify that such consent has been obtained. The Website is not directed at minors.
13. Accessibility and Transportation-Need Information
b

The Platform allows a rider, or a Customer organization on the rider's behalf, to record whether a rider requires a larger vehicle or additional wait time. The Platform does not collect diagnoses, medical records, or health conditions. These are operational settings used to assign an appropriate vehicle and schedule enough time. They are shown to the Customer's administrators, to the driver assigned to that rider's trip, and to the rider. Authorized Indro Labs staff may also access them when providing support (see Section 20).
14. Communications: SMS and Email
b

The Platform sends SMS and email notifications related to bookings, trip status, and account activity, using Twilio as the delivery provider (see Section 16). Customers choose which notifications are turned on for their organization, and riders and members can set their own notification preferences.

Under the Terms of Service, the Customer, and not Indro Labs, is the sender of these messages and is responsible for CASL compliance, including obtaining any required consent. Each SMS ends with a sender identification and an instruction to reply STOP to unsubscribe. Replying STOP (or another standard opt-out keyword) stops further SMS messages to that number and is recorded on the rider or member record; replying START re-subscribes the number. Optional notification emails include an unsubscribe link, and unsubscribing is recorded against the email address. Emails that are needed to provide the service or secure an account — for example, password-reset links, account invitations, email-verification links, and payment-failure or refund notices — do not include an unsubscribe link and are not suppressed by an unsubscribe.
15. Payments
b

Where a Customer enables payment collection for rides, payment card details are collected and stored directly by Stripe, a third-party payment processor, when the payer enters them in Stripe's hosted payment form. We do not receive or store card numbers. We keep only the reference identifiers and status information Stripe issues — such as customer, payment, payment-method, and refund identifiers, the amount, and the payment status (including any failure message) — needed to reconcile a payment with a trip.

Each Customer is liable for setting up its own Stripe account and receiving payment through it. Consistent with the Terms of Service, Indro Labs does not collect or store banking or payment information for payments between Customers, Permitted Users, and other persons, and is not involved in collecting those amounts or routing payment instructions; those payments are made directly to the payment processor. Separately, if we accept payment of our own fees under an Order Form by credit card, that payment is made through a third-party payment processor.

17. International and Cross-Border Processing
b

Although the Platform's primary hosting is located in Canada (Section 18), several of the service providers listed in Section 16 are based in, or may process information in, the United States or other countries — including Mapbox, Twilio, Stripe, Google (Fonts and other global services), Slack, and Calendly. This means personal information sent to or through those providers may be accessed, stored, or processed outside Canada, and may be subject to the laws of the jurisdiction where it is processed, including potential access by that jurisdiction's courts or authorities.
We do not represent that all personal information processed through the Platform or the Website remains in Canada at all times.
18. Canadian Data Hosting
b
The Platform's application and primary database are hosted in Google Cloud's Toronto, Ontario region.

Certain supporting infrastructure is not restricted to that region. For example, secrets-management (which stores our service credentials rather than rider, driver, or member information) uses automatic multi-region replication, and Firebase Hosting delivers the Platform's web application files through a global content-delivery network. Third-party providers are described in Sections 16 and 17.
19. Cookies, Local Storage, and Similar Technologies
b

The Platform uses your browser's local storage to keep you signed in and to avoid reloading your profile on every page. This includes your sign-in session information and a cached copy of your profile (name, email, role, organization, and photo if set). This information is stored only on your own device and is cleared when you sign out. Local storage on your device is also used for convenience settings: a driver's chosen navigation app and, for signed-in users, a short list of recently used places.

The Platform's own code does not use advertising or analytics cookies or tools. Loading the Platform's interface causes your browser to make direct requests to Google Fonts and, on map, tracking, and payment pages, to Mapbox and Stripe, which may receive your IP address and standard request information as an ordinary consequence of those requests and may use their own cookies or similar technologies under their own policies. See Section 6 for the Website.
20. Security Safeguards
b
We use a combination of technical and organizational safeguards appropriate to the information we handle, including:
Encryption of data in transit (TLS) between your browser and the Platform, and between the Platform and its database.
Password hashing, secure session management, and role-based access control limiting what each type of Platform user can see.
Isolation of each Customer organization's data from other organizations.
A production database that is not reachable from the public internet, and protected storage for service credentials.
Logging of authentication events for security monitoring.
Rate limiting on authentication and public-facing endpoints.
Restricted staff access: authorized Indro Labs staff can view a Customer's account as one of its users only for support purposes, and each such session is recorded.
No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.
21. Security Incidents
b

Under the Terms of Service, if we become aware of a breach of our security safeguards that results in the loss, theft, or unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Personal Information, we will notify the affected Customer without undue delay and provide reasonably requested assistance to the Customer in responding. If we become aware of a breach of our security safeguards involving personal information, including personal information we hold for our own purposes, we will assess the incident and take appropriate steps in accordance with applicable privacy laws. Each of Indro Labs and the Customer remains responsible for complying with its own obligations under applicable privacy law.
22. Retention and Deletion
b
We retain personal information only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this Policy, for the Customer's own operational needs, or as required by law.
What is confirmed today:
A public tracking link (Section 11) stops working 24 hours after it is created.
Only the latest position of each vehicle is stored, and it is overwritten with each update (Section 10.3).

Deactivating or suspending a rider, driver, or administrator account restricts further use of it but does not itself delete the underlying record. The Platform does not currently provide a function to permanently delete a rider, driver, or administrator account.

A Customer administrator can permanently delete a family member/caregiver record, a vehicle record, and a trip that has been scheduled but not yet assigned (and any deposit paid for such a trip is refunded first). A signed-in user can delete their own saved places.
Records of authentication events and of Terms of Service acceptance are kept as security and evidentiary records.
Platform database backups are retained for seven days, and operational logs are retained for one year.
Beyond these, the Platform does not currently run any automated process to delete or purge trip, location, or account data after a fixed period.

When a Customer's agreement ends, the Terms of Service provide that, if the Customer requests it in writing at least 30 days before the termination date and has paid all fees due, we will make its Customer Data available for electronic retrieval for 30 days and will then delete any Customer Data that remains in the systems we use to provide the Platform. We may keep Customer Data for as long as applicable law requires, and in backups, archives, and disaster-recovery systems until it is deleted in the ordinary course; it remains subject to the confidentiality requirements of the Terms of Service while we hold it.
23. Access and Correction
b

If you are an individual whose information is held through a Customer organization's use of the Platform, you should direct requests to access or correct your information to that organization in the first instance, since it determines and controls that information. Riders and drivers can also update some of their own details and notification preferences in their account settings on the Platform.

If you contact us directly, we will refer your request to the relevant Customer organization and reasonably assist that organization in responding. Under the Terms of Service, we promptly notify the Customer of any enquiry or complaint we receive from a Permitted User about their rights under privacy law (unless legally prohibited) and provide reasonably requested assistance. For personal information we hold for our own purposes (for example, information you have given us through the Website, or our own security and support records), we will respond to access and correction requests directly; you may contact us using the details in Section 26.
24. Withdrawal of Consent
b

Because consent for a Customer's own collection and use of rider, driver, or member information is obtained by the Customer organization (Section 9), a request to withdraw consent should generally be directed to that organization. We will assist a Customer organization to give effect to a valid withdrawal request where technically feasible, recognizing that withdrawing consent may mean the Customer organization can no longer provide transportation services to that individual through the Platform. Where processing is based on consent, an individual may withdraw consent, subject to legal or contractual restrictions and reasonable notice. Information may continue to be retained or used where permitted or required by law.
25. Complaints
b

If you have a concern about how personal information has been handled in connection with the Platform or the Website, you may raise it with the relevant Customer organization or contact us directly using the details in Section 26. You also have the right to file a complaint with the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, or with the privacy regulator of the applicable province, if you believe your concern has not been adequately addressed.

27. Legal Disclosures
b

We may disclose personal information where required or permitted by law — for example, in response to a court order, subpoena, or lawful request from a government or regulatory authority, or where necessary to investigate suspected fraud, security incidents, or violations of our agreements. We may also disclose information to potential assignees, acquirers, or successors in connection with a proposed or actual sale, merger, or other corporate transaction involving our business or assets, subject to confidentiality obligations.
28. Changes to This Policy
b

We may update this Policy from time to time by posting the updated version on the Website with a revised “Last updated” date. Where applicable law requires us to give you notice of a change, we will do so.
29. Effective Date
b
